title: Solo Grinding update Does this way of showing status/buffs icons work?
author: Far-Comedian-5703
selftext:
Hey guys! My first post here about my project got a really warm welcome here, so thanks a lot for that ;) Wanted to show you a quick look at some status effects and buffs I’ve added to game,  also wanted to ask more experienced devs how to display these icons. Right now, they show up under turn order slot, and you can hover over them to see description. They also appear above the enemy tooltip when you hover over a unit if you hold CTRL, the tooltip stays pinned so you can move your mouse over the icons to read what they do  
Does this setup look alright, or would you change  something how icons are shown?  
As for how status effects works, some statuses cancel each other out  for example, if  enemy is Burning and you hit it with  skill who apply Wet, burning is gone. Same with Burning and Rooted. Some also need a specific status to trigger something else. For example, you can only Freeze someone if they’re already Wet and if they are Paralyzed and you apply Wet, it triggers Stun. I’ve got 9 statuses so far.  Don’t want to add too many though, I want them to be more like  bonus/utility thing rather than making the whole gameplay just about statuses ;D

comments.body: looks great, how did you do those status vfx?

replies.author: Far-Comedian-5703
replies.body: Got them from the Asset Store, but man, it took ages to set up properly. Had a lot of issues with rendering and getting the angles right so they align with the tiles. Some of them still look a bit off, so I need to tweak the settings more

replies.author: Far-Comedian-5703
replies.body: Yeah, effects there are  amazing, and you can  tweak them manually in Unity. I checked once how making such an effect looks like, those guys are doing an amazing job ;D

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Looks great. Maybe only show the heads of your sprite as thumbnail icons for the turns? Just zoom in on the heads instead of showing the entire body

replies.author: Far-Comedian-5703
replies.body: Actually was thinking about making them animated (idle) instead of just static sprites, but I will check how it looks with zoomed heads. Didn't think of that, thanks for the tip! :D

comments.author: surpurdurd
comments.body: Looks good. I might tighten up the vfx a little so they don't overlap like crazy when units are adjacent, try to keep the effect local to just that square and no wider. Also I might lengthen the delay on the tooltip pop-ups or give it a fade-in effect or something, but that's just personal taste, something you might include as an adjustable option in the settings.

replies.author: Far-Comedian-5703
replies.body: Oh, didn't notice I actually don't have a lock to wait for the first animation to finish before starting next one, so that's why they overlap. Thanks ;D About  VFX  I thought it looked better when it's not strictly 'locked' in tile  to make it feel less stiff, but I'll play around with it and see how it looks. And yeah, settings for little tooltip delay is a great idea. Thanks for the feedback getting right on it;)

comments.body: I have actually been following. Loving to see you are making progress. Im curious what AI pixel art generator did you use for you characters/idle animations?

replies.body: Thanks! I used [ludo.ai](http://ludo.ai) for the player/enemy/npc animations ;)

comments.author: UltraLNSS
comments.body: Ohh, I didn't see this one before. Been wanting to do a SRPG for a long time. How difficult is it?

replies.author: Far-Comedian-5703
replies.body:
You know game Dofus or Wakfu? I’ve been playing them since I was a kid and I keep coming back to them they’re a huge inspiration for me. I figured a solo Rogulite experience with a heavy focus on character building would fit this style perfectly ;D

It’s hard for me to say exactly how difficult it is since this is my first project and I’m basically learning as I go. For example when first time I tried making a cutscene I hated it so much I almost decided the game wouldn't have any cutscenes at all lol. But now it’s actually going pretty well, same with other things. The hardest part is making sure everything works together. I’m trying to set it all up so that adding new content later is easy.The biggest challenge will definitely be balancing. In my opinion, balancing this genre as a solo dev is hell. Marketing and getting people to test the game is also tough for me. tried to limit the use of AI to a minimum where I absolutely had to (npc/enemy/player animations), but I'm already in that 'lower sort' of games drawer anyway. Currently, I'm finishing up the starting area for some playtests on my Discord. We’ll see how it goes,  most important thing is that I’m having a lot fun creating this! ;D
